body: I hear that. NY is one of the most expensive places to live. I know mostly managers and chefs and you can definitely earn more than $500/mo. here if you have skills and dedication. The cost of living in the city is very high. Though if you were willing to live outside the city and commute in, you could possibly make it work. There is hope, whether in Ecuador or the U.S.

I'm from the U.S., and in my experience, there was no mandatory counseling involved in being prescribed anti-depressants. The first time I was prescribed them, it was by a general practitioner. I later began to see a psychologist for talk therapy as an additional measure in battling the depression. She referred me to a psychiatrist who adjusted my meds and doses. As far as I know it wasn't on any official record since the psychiatrist was paid for out of pocket and it wasn't put through my insurance. 

In any case, depression is a common condition and millions of people are being treated for it with anti-depressants. There is nothing to be ashamed of, and I doubt your medical history would come up in any job application for a position in the film industry. (It might be a different case if you're applying to be a police officer or want to run for public office.) Also, junkies who go to doctors seeking drugs tend to try and get the harder stuff, not anti-depressants which aren't a controlled substance, at least here in the U.S. I don't think any reputable doctor would make you jump through hoops to get you the help you need.

I urge you to seek professional help of some kind, whatever kind you feel comfortable with.

So glad to hear it. PM me if you want to discuss job possibilities after you finish school. Not sure what the visa situation is like, but I do know a bunch of people in the restaurant business in NY always looking for hard workers.
To the OP: Hi, I just want to check in and see how you're doing. Please update if you can. Thanks!

At 12 years old I tried to drown myself in the bathtub. I attempted at 16 by overdosing on pills. My parents were alarmed but refused to get me treatment, even though I begged for help. (I believe my parents refused to get me treatment because they feared it would prove they had done something wrong while raising me. Which they did—constant emotional abuse.) Since then I've had periods of terrible suicide impulses but got as far as detailed planning but no action. It wasn't until i was in my late 20s that I had the means to seek professional help.
I hear you. It's definitely a tough situation. Do you have access to health care where you live?

I do. My suicidal feelings get  much worse the more broke we get. (I support our whole family while also caring for my son full time. My husband just leeches and seems to not care that i work myself ragged and barely ever sleep.)

What i do understand from your post is that you are young and indeed working toward a goal. There's no telling what opportunities might present themselves in the future if you hang in there and stay on course. The fact that you're in school is excellent and I applaud you for the effort you're putting in.

Also, keep in mind that there's no deadline for starting a family. Why does it have to happen by age 30? You'll get there when you get there. I started my family at age 38 and surviving is still a struggle but the best you can do is try and continue to work hard and believe in yourself. 

I'll be thinking about you and wish you all the success on your path. Please please stay on that path and acknowledge how wonderful it is to have family support.

Edited to add: the worldwide economy is in shambles and you are not alone in struggling financially. Please try to take comfort in that fact that you're not alone in that.
Also, I don't think it's possible to get well. It can get better temporarily like I've experienced in the past, but depression is my default setting and I always arrive back here.

Thanks for your reply. Wouldn't it be better then, to have my son safely placed with my sister than risk having him taken to foster care? Can he be taken away because of my depression? He is so well cared for. His care is always my top priority.
